:::{#exm-homogeneous-function}
#### Homogeneous functions, and one that is not

- $f(x) = 2x$ on $\reals$ is [homogeneous](#def-homogeneous-function). For $x, c \in \reals$:

  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  f(c x) &= 2 c x \\
  &= c (2x) \\
  &= c f(x)
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- $h(x) = x^2$ on $\reals$ is not homogeneous,
  since $h(2 \cd 1) = 4$ but $2\,h(1) = 2$.

- $k(\vx) = \paren{x_1^3 + x_2^3}^{1/3}$ on $\reals^2$, with the real cube root, is homogeneous but not [additive](#def-additive-function).
  For $\vx \in \reals^2$ and $c \in \reals$:

  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  k(c \vx) &= \paren{c^3 x_1^3 + c^3 x_2^3}^{1/3} \\
  &= \paren{c^3 \paren{x_1^3 + x_2^3}}^{1/3} \\
  &= c \paren{x_1^3 + x_2^3}^{1/3} \\
  &= c\, k(\vx)
  \end{aligned}
  $$

  but $k((1, 0) + (0, 1)) = k((1, 1)) = 2^{1/3}$,
  while $k((1, 0)) + k((0, 1)) = 2$.

<!-- no-figure: the example checks an algebraic identity; it has no data or fitted model to plot -->

:::
